samples.question: This image shows one small framed box labelled KEY standing alone above a row of five larger framed panels of identical size, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. The KEY box holds a single figure. Every panel holds exactly four figures. Every figure in the image, including the key, is an outlined silhouette whose inside is filled with straight parallel stripes, and all outlines enclose the same amount of area, so size, figure count and total ink carry no information. Figures are drawn in several colours and colour is never informative: a figure never has to share the key's colour to match it. An outline is never rotated and never mirrored anywhere in the image, so two figures share an outline exactly when one could be slid over the other and cover it. The stripes inside a figure run in one of four directions: flat across, upright, or slanted one way or the other. A figure matches the key only if it satisfies both conditions at once: the same outline as the key and the same stripe direction as the key. In every one of the five panels exactly two of the four figures repeat the key's outline and exactly two of the four figures repeat the key's stripe direction, so counting figures that share only the outline, or only the stripe direction, gives the same answer of two in every panel and never separates them. In exactly one panel a single figure carries both key features together; in the other four panels no figure does, and there every figure that repeats the key's outline has stripes running at least a quarter turn away from the key's stripes, while every figure that repeats the key's stripe direction has a visibly different outline. Which numbered panel contains the figure that matches the key in both outline and stripe direction? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
